title: Open Standard OUSD: SBI–Coinbase shared network, Bridge issuance, Circle/Ripple competition and reserve-data reconciliation

append_only.purpose: Resolve the SBI/Coinbase relationship through Open Standard, distinguish OUSD from USDC/RLUSD, and preserve conflicting official reserve metrics.

source_capture_policy.reason: Official company and reserve pages were reviewed through rendered extracts; byte-complete captures and independent timestamp receipts were not preserved.

claims_supported: SBI Holdings and Startale joined Open Standard.
The announcement names Coinbase among the 140+ participating companies.
SBI and Startale said they would explore a JPYSC–OUSD interoperability proof of concept.
The announcement explicitly says the release is pilot exploration only, not a new service or production settlement/trading launch.
limitations: The SBI release's 140+ participant count differs from later Open Standard/Startale pages reporting 200+; date and definition may differ.
No production settlement volume, actual capital transfer, or XRP use is disclosed.

claims_supported: Startale describes Open Standard as an alliance of 200+ companies including Visa, Stripe, Mastercard, BlackRock and Coinbase.
SBI/Startale are exploring JPYSC–OUSD interoperability, not operating a production service.
limitations: Startale is a project participant and its ecosystem claims are not independent transaction-volume measurements.

claims_supported: OUSD is issued by Bridge, a Stripe company, for Open Standard.
The page describes OUSD as fully reserved, free to issue/redeem 1:1, and live on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo.
The page displays 200+ network partners and lists Coinbase and SBI Holdings.
The page says reserve income flows to Open Standard partners after a management fee.
The page displays $468M in circulation and says the reserve mix was 54.9% cash and 45.1% short-dated U.S. Treasuries as of October 2026.
limitations: The $468M metric has no precise as-of timestamp on the page.
The page also advertises a November 12, 2026 first-live-payments/opening event, which is future relative to this research cutoff; do not treat that event as already completed.
The displayed reserve mix is not accompanied on this page by a current independent attestation.

claims_supported: OUSD supply: 910,426,478.
Reserve assets: $912,426,596; displayed overcollateralization: $2,000,117 and 100.22% coverage.
The dashboard lists only an August 2026 attestation report.
limitations: Live dashboard values are issuer/administrator telemetry, not an independent current attestation.

The cash and Treasury line items sum to $910,426,481, approximately the supply, not the displayed $912,426,596 reserve total; the $2,000,115 surplus is not separately allocated in the displayed breakdown.
The dashboard's current supply differs materially from the Open Standard marketing page's $468M circulation figure; the marketing page lacks an exact timestamp, so do not average the values.
The listed August attestation predates the September 30 launch and is not evidence for November balances.

claims_supported: OUSD was announced live on Solana on September 30, 2026.
The announcement says Bridge issues OUSD and identifies reserves at BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY.
The five founding partners are Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa; the post says they committed more than $1B to OUSD liquidity.
The post describes a broader network of more than 200 companies, including SBI Holdings.
limitations: Partner announcement; committed liquidity is not the same as fully deployed circulating supply or actual settlement volume.
No XRPL or XRP usage is described.

claims_supported: Coinbase made RLUSD available through Prime, Exchange and Retail in supported regions.
At launch, deposits and withdrawals are supported across XRPL, Base and Ethereum.
Coinbase Global Exchange collateral use was described as a future capability, not live at launch.
Ripple said it would provide liquidity on Base.
limitations: This is a distribution announcement, not evidence of XRP bridge volume, XRP purchases or actual RLUSD settlement volume.

source_registry.publisher: SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank
claims_supported: SBI Holdings acquired $25M of Circle shares and SBI Shinsei Bank acquired $25M, for $50M combined strategic investment.
SBI and Circle signed a comprehensive business alliance MOU in November 2023.
SBI VC Trade began retail USDC handling in Japan in March 2025.
SBI and Circle signed an agreement to establish SBI Circle Holdings.
limitations: Equity investment is historical capital deployed, not a current XRP investment.
No XRP use or XRP collateral is implied by USDC distribution.

source_registry.publisher: SBI Holdings, SBI VC Trade, Ripple and Standard Custody
claims_supported: SBI VC Trade and Standard Custody & Trust Company, a Ripple subsidiary and RLUSD issuer, signed an MOU for RLUSD issuance/distribution in Japan.
The release describes RLUSD as backed by USD deposits, short-term U.S. Treasuries and cash equivalents.
limitations: MOU is a commercial relationship, not a disclosed XRP purchase or XRP collateral arrangement.

claims_supported: Coinbase states that its Circle arrangement was renewed on the same terms.
Coinbase Q3 revenue concentration disclosure says one counterparty accounted for 27% of total revenue; the reviewed passage does not identify it.
limitations: Do not attribute the unnamed counterparty to Circle.
Issuer filing is not independent proof of actual USDC payment volume.

direct_vs_indirect_findings.explanation: SBI Holdings and Coinbase are both in Open Standard, but no direct bilateral SBI–Coinbase contract was found. SBI invested in Circle and distributes USDC; Coinbase has a Circle distribution/equity relationship. Separately, SBI VC Trade has an RLUSD relationship with Ripple/Standard Custody while Coinbase distributes RLUSD globally. These are shared counterparties and consortium links, not proof of a direct SBI–Coinbase commercial agreement.

xrp_implications.substitution_hypothesis: OUSD offers a dollar-denominated, multi-chain payment/settlement asset with partner-shared reserve economics and Coinbase distribution. It may compete with XRP as a bridge/settlement asset in some corridors, especially where users can settle directly in USD stablecoins.
xrp_implications.complementarity_hypothesis: OUSD and JPYSC may create yen-dollar on-chain liquidity that increases tokenized-asset and cross-border activity; XRP could still serve separate liquidity or bridge functions if a route actually uses it.
disconfirming_evidence_needed: XRPL/OUSD native contract or bridge deployment evidence
Transaction-level payment route showing XRP as an intermediary
Net XRP order flow attributable to OUSD/JPYSC corridors
Production JPYSC–OUSD pilot launch and measured settlement volumes
xrp_implications.current_status: No XRP or XRPL deployment, XRP collateral use, or XRP transaction volume was disclosed in the reviewed OUSD/SBI materials.

reserve_data_disagreement.reconciliation: The marketing-page circulation metric and reserve mix are materially different from Bridge's November 5 live dashboard. The marketing page has no precise timestamp; the dashboard is timestamped but issuer-operated. Treat the marketing values as stale/undated or definitionally different until an exact dated reconciliation is published. Do not average.
reserve_data_disagreement.reserve_breakdown_arithmetic: Bridge's displayed cash plus Treasury amounts total $910,426,481, while the displayed reserve total is $912,426,596; the $2,000,115 surplus is not separately allocated in the displayed asset-type breakdown.

evidence_limits: Bridge's current dashboard is not a current independent attestation.
The only attestation link displayed by Bridge is August 2026, before the September 30 launch; it is not used to infer current balances.
OUSD marketing-page and Bridge dashboard metrics conflict and have different timestamp quality.
SBI/Startale JPYSC–OUSD work is pilot exploration, not production settlement.
Open Standard partner membership does not establish bilateral agreements among all members.
No XRP-specific adoption, collateral, purchase or settlement volume is established.

admission_decision.reason: Rendered sources, conflicting supply vintages, no raw receipts, and no transaction-level XRP linkage.
